$comment: Source-of-truth mapping from upstream AWS skill repos (under reference/) to TalkOps agent and vertical plugins. Consumed by scripts/sync_aws_plugins.py. Hand-authored files (agents/<name>.md in agent plugins, commands/*.md in vertical plugins) are never overwritten by the sync.

metadata.description: DevOps and cloud-operations plugins for AI agents. Agent plugins bind skills, commands, hooks, and MCP servers to a named specialist agent; vertical plugins apply skills to the main agent; partner-built plugins wrap third-party integrations.

hosts.$comment: Per-host packaging. The sync always writes the Claude Code layout (.claude-plugin/plugin.json, .mcp.json, agents/, hooks/hooks.json) and the portable Agent Plugins 1.0.0 layout (plugin.json, mcp.json, skills/) plus the Codex overlay (.codex-plugin/plugin.json) and the Codex marketplace (.agents/plugins/marketplace.json).

aws-mcp.$comment: Managed AWS MCP Server via the toolkit's pinned proxy (aws___call_aws, aws___search_documentation, aws___retrieve_skill, ...).

aws-mcp-legacy-proxy.$comment: Managed AWS MCP Server via the proxy used by awslabs/agent-plugins.

iam.$comment: Read-only by default (the server only mutates with --allow-write). Add --allow-write to allow IAM mutations.

eks.$comment: Read-only by default. Add --allow-write / --allow-sensitive-data-access to enable mutations and pod logs/secrets.

ecs.$comment: Read-only by default. Set ALLOW_WRITE / ALLOW_SENSITIVE_DATA to true to enable mutations. fastmcp<4 pin: upstream needs fastmcp>=3.2 and is not yet compatible with fastmcp 4.

dataprocessing.$comment: Read-only by default. Add --allow-write to let the agent create/modify Glue, EMR, and Athena resources.

s3tables.$comment: Read-only by default. Add --allow-write to enable table creation and appends.

sagemaker.$comment: Read-only by default. Add --allow-write / --allow-sensitive-data-access to enable mutations.

sns-sqs.$comment: Manages SNS topics and SQS queues. Creating topics/queues is off by default (add --allow-resource-creation).

mq.$comment: Manages Amazon MQ (RabbitMQ/ActiveMQ) brokers. Broker creation is off by default (add --allow-resource-creation).

elasticache.$comment: ElastiCache control plane, read-only. Remove --readonly to allow create/modify/delete.

postgres.$comment: Aurora/RDS PostgreSQL, read-only (no --allow_write_query). Pick the cluster at runtime with the connect_to_database tool; use a read-only database role.

mysql.$comment: Aurora/RDS MySQL, read-only (no --allow_write_query). Pick the cluster at runtime with the connect_to_database tool; use a read-only database user.

finch.$comment: Builds and pushes container images with the local Finch CLI. ECR repository creation is off by default (add --enable-aws-resource-write).

appsync.$comment: AWS AppSync APIs, read-only by default. Add --allow-write to create APIs, data sources, and resolvers.

aws-serverless-mcp.$comment: SAM/Lambda/ESM guidance and inspection, read-only. Add --allow-write to deploy and --allow-sensitive-data-access for logs.

spark-troubleshooting.$comment: Managed remote MCP (SageMaker Unified Studio) that diagnoses failed Spark jobs on EMR, Glue, and SageMaker notebooks. Uses your AWS credentials via SigV4.

spark-upgrade.$comment: Managed remote MCP (SageMaker Unified Studio) that plans and validates Spark version upgrades on EMR. Uses your AWS credentials via SigV4.

aws-mcp-read-only.$comment: Managed AWS MCP Server, read-only: the proxy's --read-only flag drops every tool whose readOnlyHint is not true (aws___call_aws, aws___run_script, aws___get_presigned_url), leaving documentation, regional availability, and skill retrieval.

aurora-dsql.purpose: Schema inspection, read-only queries, and (opt-in) transactions on one Aurora DSQL cluster.
aurora-dsql.notes: Read-only by default; append `--allow-writes` to enable `transact`. The `dsql` skill's scripts work without this connector.

documentdb.purpose: Query and inspect Amazon DocumentDB collections.
documentdb.notes: Read-only unless you add `--allow-write`. Keep the connection string out of shared project config.

keyspaces.purpose: Explore keyspaces/tables and run CQL against Amazon Keyspaces or Apache Cassandra.
keyspaces.notes: Connection settings live in `~/.keyspaces-mcp/env` (see upstream docs for Cassandra and TLS options).

neptune.purpose: Status, schema, and openCypher/Gremlin queries on Neptune Database or Neptune Analytics.

valkey.purpose: Read (and opt-in write) data in an ElastiCache/MemoryDB Valkey or Redis OSS cache.
valkey.notes: Drop `--readonly` only for caches you are allowed to mutate.

memcached.purpose: Read (and opt-in write) data in an ElastiCache Memcached cluster.

mssql.purpose: Schema inspection and queries on one RDS for SQL Server instance.
mssql.notes: Bind a Secrets Manager secret for a read-only login with `--secret_arn`.

oracle.purpose: Schema inspection and queries on RDS for Oracle or Oracle Database@AWS.
oracle.notes: Default TCPS port is 2484; see upstream docs for Autonomous Database and Exadata.

timestream-influxdb.purpose: Manage Timestream for InfluxDB instances and query/write InfluxDB data.

lambda-tool.purpose: Expose selected Lambda functions as MCP tools the agent can invoke.
lambda-tool.notes: Always scope with `FUNCTION_PREFIX`, `FUNCTION_LIST`, or `FUNCTION_TAG_KEY`/`FUNCTION_TAG_VALUE`; unfiltered it exposes every function in the account.

stepfunctions-tool.purpose: Expose selected Step Functions state machines as MCP tools the agent can start.
stepfunctions-tool.notes: Always scope with `STATE_MACHINE_PREFIX`, `STATE_MACHINE_LIST`, or a tag filter.

terraform.purpose: Live Terraform Registry lookups: provider resource/data-source docs, module search and inputs, and Sentinel/policy libraries.
terraform.notes: Needs Docker (or swap in the release binary: `terraform-mcp-server stdio`). Without `TFE_TOKEN` it exposes only public-registry lookups, which is all the agent needs. Do not add `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS=true`: the agent runs `terraform plan`/`apply` itself so every change goes through the approval gate.

mcp_upstream_index.$comment: Every server directory in awslabs/mcp (reference/mcp/src) mapped to the mcp_catalog/connector_catalog key that uses it, or a reason it is not used. scripts/sync_aws_plugins.py renders docs/mcp-server-coverage.md from this and fails if a directory is unmapped.

amazon-qindex-mcp-server.skip: Q index access for ISVs; not cloud operations.

aws-bedrock-custom-model-import-mcp-serv.skip: Niche model-import workflow; Bedrock work goes through `aws-mcp` and the Bedrock skills.

aws-documentation-mcp-server.skip: Superseded by the AWS Knowledge MCP server (`awsknowledge`) and `aws___search_documentation`.

aws-for-sap-management-mcp-server.skip: SAP-specific operations; candidate for a future SAP vertical or partner plugin.

aws-healthomics-mcp-server.skip: Healthcare and life-sciences domain server; out of scope for cloud operations.

aws-iot-sitewise-mcp-server.skip: Industrial IoT domain server; out of scope for cloud operations.

bedrock-kb-retrieval-mcp-server.skip: Queries a specific Bedrock knowledge base; application-level and needs KB IDs.

ccapi-mcp-server.skip: Deprecated upstream in favour of aws-iac-mcp-server (`awsiac`).

document-loader-mcp-server.skip: Generic document parsing (PDF, Office); not AWS operations.

healthimaging-mcp-server.skip: Healthcare and life-sciences domain server; out of scope for cloud operations.

healthlake-mcp-server.skip: Healthcare and life-sciences domain server; out of scope for cloud operations.

mcp-lambda-handler.skip: Python library for hosting MCP servers on Lambda, not a server.

openapi-mcp-server.skip: Generic OpenAPI-to-MCP bridge that needs a target API spec; candidate for partner-built plugins.

roda-mcp-server.skip: Discovers public datasets in the Registry of Open Data on AWS; not cloud operations.

security-agent-mcp-server.skip: AWS Security Agent is not allowlisted for the DevOps Plugins scope.

hooks.prompt: A DSQL transact operation completed. Verify the result: if it was a DDL change, confirm the schema looks correct using get_schema. If it was a DML change, confirm the affected row count is expected. If it was an EXPLAIN operation, follow up on Query Plan Explainability within the DSQL skill

aws-mutation-gate.$comment: Classifies AWS-mutating shell commands (aws, terraform, cdk, sam, eksctl, kubectl, helm) and aws___call_aws/aws___run_script calls. Claude Code: deny for aws_read_only agents, ask otherwise. Codex (no agent identity in hook input): adds a warning to the model context. TALKOPS_AWS_MUTATION_GATE=off|warn|ask|deny overrides the default.

hooks.command: sh -c 'command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec python3 "$0"; command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec python "$0"; exec py -3 "$0"' "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/aws-mutation-gate.py"
sh -c 'command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec python3 "$0"; command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec python "$0"; exec py -3 "$0"' "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/aws-mutation-gate.py"
